name: DeepSeek-V3
attention_variant: MLA (multi-head latent attention), q_lora_rank 1536, kv_lora_rank 512, 128 heads expanded from latent
license: DeepSeek Model License (bespoke; permits commercial use, restricts some uses)
notes:
MLA, and the reason this record matters for serving: the resident KV is a 512-rank latent, not per-head K/V. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 61 layers x (kv_lora_rank 512 + qk_rope_head_dim 64) x 2 bytes (bf16) = 61 x 576 x 2 = 70,272 B/token (68.6 KiB). Do NOT apply the standard GQA formula here: num_layers x num_kv_heads x head_dim x 2 x 2 would give 61 x 128 x 128 x 2 x 2 = 4,000,256 B/token, overstating by 57x. config.json lists num_key_value_heads 128 because the latent is expanded to 128 heads at attention time, not because 128 head-pairs are cached. Params: vendor card states 671B total / 37B activated; the HF safetensors total is 684.53B (includes the MTP layer, num_nextn_predict_layers 1). Our own arithmetic from config gives 670.9B total / 37.4B active, which matches the vendor active figure to 1%. MoE: 256 routed + 1 always-on shared expert, 8 per token, first_k_dense_replace 3 (layers 0-2 are dense, not MoE), n_group 8 / topk_group 4 grouped routing. Context: max_position_embeddings 163840 via YaRN rope_scaling factor 40 over an original 4096, rope_theta 10000. Serving note: bf16 weights are ~1.37 TB, so this is an FP8/FP4-only proposition in practice.

SERVICEABILITY JOIN (added 2026-10-03; the architecture x engine matrix this record was missing, with a citation per cell in docs/13-model-compatibility.md): FAMILY=mla. REQUIRED KERNEL CLASS: an MLA decode kernel. MLA is not a variant of the GQA kernel - the cache is a shared low-rank latent (d_c) plus a decoupled RoPE key, not per-head K/V, so an engine that lacks a dedicated MLA decode path cannot serve the class at all. SUPPORTED BY (cited): vLLM native rows DeepseekV2ForCausalLM, DeepseekV3ForCausalLM, DeepseekV32ForCausalLM, DeepseekV4ForCausalLM [[mdl2-vllm-supported-models-2026-10]]; TensorRT-LLM the same four rows plus GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM (GLM-5), Glm4MoeForCausalLM (GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7), KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration and KimiLinearForCausalLM [[mdl2-trtllm-supported-models]]; SGLang generative table names DeepSeek v1/v2/v3/R1 and Kimi K2 as supported [[mdl2-sglang-generative-models]]; llama.cpp reaches MLA through the DEEPSEEK2/DEEPSEEK32/DEEPSEEK4 arch entries, which are in its supports_sm_tensor == false list, i.e. no tensor-core matmul path for the attention itself [[mdl2-llamacpp-arch-class-registry]]; ik-llama-cpp records MLA as a feature that landed there first and was later upstreamed [[ik-llama-cpp]].ENGINE KERNEL CONSTRAINTS THAT CHANGE WHAT THE ENGINE MUST STORE (this is the important class of fact): (1) FlashInfer, which is SGLang's default attention backend and selectable in vLLM [[flashinfer]], is where the MLA decode kernels live, and they are instantiated per KV cache page-block size: gotcha-sm120-sparse-mla-block-size records vLLM computing compressed-layer pbs = block_size // compress_ratio (= 32 at block_size 64 for a ratio-2 layer) while FlashInfer's SM120 planner hard-codes _PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE = 64, so DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash will not start on 8x RTX PRO 6000 at TP8 at ANY global block size (64 gives pbs=32 and crashes; 128 gives 'No common block size'). Workaround is SM100 datacenter Blackwell or a FlashInfer planner change. (2) FlashMLA's 2026.09.30 release requires SM100/SM103 and CUDA >= 13.1, REMOVED Hopper support and removed V3/V3.2/V4.0, and supports ONLY FP8 and FP4 KV cache - unquantized bfloat16 KV is explicitly not supported [[kern-flashmla-github]]. So the kernel choice decides the KV CACHE FORMAT: to use that decode kernel the engine must store an FP8/FP4 latent with per-token inlined scales, and V4.1's layout is 528 bytes/token (512 of float8_e4m3 over all 512 dims - the 64 RoPE dims are quantized too, no bf16 part - plus 16 bytes of float8_e8m0 scales, one per 32 e4m3 values), with an fp4 variant at 288 bytes/token [[flashmla-decode-fp8-fp4-kv]]. A Hopper box therefore cannot take that kernel and an engine that only offers bf16 MLA KV cannot take it either. (3) Independent of the kernel: TRT-LLM's MLA rows carry two footnotes that constrain serving rather than correctness - chunked prefill for MLA only enables on SM90/SM100/SM103/SM107/SM120, and KV cache reuse for MLA only enables on SM90/100/103/107/120/121 in BF16/FP8 [[mdl2-trtllm-supported-models]]. (4) TRT-LLM states DeepSeek-V4 is Blackwell SM100+ only and Kimi K3 is SM100 family only, with a worked recipe split (DEP16 needs GB300-class per-GPU memory, TEP16 validated on GB200) [[mdl2-trtllm-supported-models]]. ISA CONSEQUENCE: at 68.6 KiB/token MLA moves the bottleneck off KV and onto weight streaming, so MLA-capable engines find their paged-attention machinery largely idle and their GQA-era cache-pressure tuning irrelevant [[mla-latent-attention]].  TRT-LLM footnotes specific to this checkpoint: chunked prefill for MLA only enables on SM90/SM100/SM103/SM107/SM120 and KV cache reuse for MLA only on SM90/100/103/107/120/121 in BF16/FP8 KV dtype [[mdl2-trtllm-supported-models]]. On Hopper, FlashMLA is no longer an option at the 2026.09.30 release (Hopper support removed), so the MLA decode kernel must come from elsewhere and the bf16 KV cache stays [[kern-flashmla-github]].

CONTEXT_SCALING_METHOD (yarn): config-derived; the existing free text 'YaRN (factor 40, original 4096)' agrees.
